key_insight: Dense Fe-based amorphous coatings with fewer pores show better long-term corrosion resistance, while higher humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce protective coatings for carbon-steel components exposed to corrosion and sliding wear.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, lamellar structure, and coating defects.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and sliding wear under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links greater porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates with increasing humidity.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear findings involve Si3N4 counterbodies and may not generalize to other contact materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
